answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a vault before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. The protocol caps influence by locked stake and lets counterparties slash that stake when an agent fails an auditable obligation, such as delivering a valid result by a deadline. Creating a thousand identities then requires a thousand funded deposits, not merely new keys; the attacker ties up capital and risks losing it. A knoll of reputation or a jetty of referrals cannot bypass the stake requirement.
